justification: Changes which pages the production AI reader extracts provisions from. For a chapter sharing a PDF, rules were read from the whole file and credited to the chapter; after this, only its own page range is read. Wrong pages here means wrong rules served.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-10-25: Railway dcp-extract (AI_MODEL=sol) logged 'shares its PDF; extracting pages 52-79 only' for Bayside s3-5 (34.9 MB, 236-page Part 3 PDF), then the new per-call [reader] line never appeared in 69+ min. DCPExtractor.page_range is honoured by _owned_pages (regex reader) but dcp_extract_changed.py:1907 called ai_extract_chapter without it.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The preflight message promised a page slice that the LLM reader never received: it chunked all 236 pages from page 1, and both re-read passes judged every page of the shared file as this chapter's.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: ai_extract_chapter takes page_range (1-based inclusive), clamped exactly like _owned_pages; chunks, page-coverage re-read and sentence re-read stay inside it; page numbers keep meaning the page in the file. No range = whole file, as before.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No new external call. Fewer pages are sent to the provider.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change; provisions keep the same page numbering.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a shared-PDF chapter extracted by the LLM reader could carry other chapters' rules (wrong rules shown for an address) or never finish. After: only its own pages; a stale range end is clamped, not refused, as the regex reader does.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest -q -o addopts= tests/test_ai_extractor.py tests/test_ai_chunk_loss.py tests/test_ai_extractor_sentence_coverage.py tests/test_shared_pdf_page_slicing.py tests/test_dcp_extract_ai_page_range.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: the reader chunks pages outside the range, either re-read offers another chapter's pages, the range is not clamped, or the extractor stops passing page_range
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES: 6 hand-made mutants (chunk whole file, drop page-coverage filter, drop sentence filter, no clamp, no fail-closed on an empty range, caller drops page_range), each killed. Sol cross-review found the empty-range silent success; fixed.

functions.name: ai_extract_chapter
functions.input: pdf path, council, model and the optional chapter page range from the registry row
functions.output: section dicts from the owned pages only, page numbers as in the file
functions.if_none: page_range None reads the whole file exactly as before this change

functions.name: owned_span
functions.input: the optional page range and the file's total page count
functions.output: the first and last owned page numbers, clamped to the file's 1..total pages
functions.if_none: a None page range gives the whole file, pages 1 to total

functions.name: _reread_skipped_pages
functions.input: pdf path, reader, model, provisions so far and the owned page span
functions.output: re-reads only owned pages the first pass left out
functions.if_none: owned None keeps every page of the file, exactly as before

functions.name: _reread_missing_sentences
functions.input: pdf path, reader, model, provisions so far and the owned page span
functions.output: checks and re-reads sentences on owned pages only
functions.if_none: owned None keeps every page of the file, exactly as before

break_it.scenario: Bayside s3-5: pages 52-79 of a 236-page shared PDF
break_it.what_happens: three chunks are read, pages 52-63, 64-75 and 76-79, and nothing outside them

break_it.scenario: Registry says 8-25 but the file has 20 pages
break_it.what_happens: pages 8 to 20 are read, the same clamp the regex reader applies

break_it.scenario: Page-coverage re-read sees other chapters' pages as 'left out'
break_it.what_happens: only pages 52 to 79 are offered for a second reading, never other chapters
break_it.how: lines filtered to owned before skipped_pages

break_it.scenario: Running header detection from a 28-page slice is weaker
break_it.what_happens: running lines still computed from every page of the file before filtering
break_it.how: pc.running_lines(lines) runs before the owned filter

break_it.scenario: A chapter that owns the whole file (no page_range on its registry row)
break_it.what_happens: reads every page from page 1, identical to before

break_it.scenario: Sol: a range that misses the file (250-260 of 236 pages, or 79-52 reversed)
break_it.what_happens: ValueError 'holds no page of this PDF' is raised, so the chapter fails visibly instead of returning no rules
break_it.how: owned_span raises when a given range clamps to lo > hi

break_it.scenario: Sol advisory: a zero-page PDF with no page_range
break_it.what_happens: unchanged from before this PR: no chunks are read; the downstream completeness guard compares against live rows
break_it.how: verdict: pre-existing, out of scope for a page-range fix; not widened here
break_it.repro: ai_extract_chapter on a 0-page reader with page_range None
